headline: 10 killed in Cox's Bazar resort fire: Police sue resort owner, manager arrested
summary: A case has been filed against 23 people, including the owner of Tup-Tup Resort, after a devastating blaze claimed 10 lives in Ukhiya.
details: At least 10 people were killed when a massive blaze ripped through the Tup-Tup Resort in the Patuattek area of Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar. Four of the victims were found dead in two bathrooms on the third floor.
Police have filed a case against 23 people, with the resort owner, Md. Tanvir, named as the primary accused. The resort manager, Zahidul Islam, has already been arrested from the scene.

Fire service officials revealed that the wooden resort lacked basic fire safety equipment, including portable extinguishers, fire alarms, and hose pipes. The establishment also operated without a fire license.
The fire broke out around 7:30 AM on Saturday and spread rapidly due to strong sea breezes and the wooden structure of the building. It was brought under control by 8:15 AM.

Of the 10 deceased, six have been identified, including five women and a five-year-old child. The victims include residents of Dhaka's Banashree and Khilgaon areas, as well as a resident of Chuadanga.
Cox's Bazar Police Superintendent A N M Sajeedur Rahman stated that an investigation is ongoing to determine the exact cause of the fire.

headline: DMP orders probe into State Minister Ishraque's display of firearms
summary: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police have launched an investigation after videos surfaced of the State Minister for Liberation War Affairs brandishing guns during an 'anti-drug' drive.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has ordered an investigation into the brandishing of firearms by State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain and his associates.
The probe follows videos uploaded by the minister himself to his verified Facebook page, showing him carrying a firearm while chasing people during a drive in Gandaria.
DMP Detective Branch chief Shafiqul Islam stated that the deputy commissioner of the DMP's Wari Division has been assigned to investigate the incident.
In one video, captioned 'Ishraque's action: Drug dens demolished, dealers handed over to police', the minister and another individual were seen carrying firearms.
Another video showed police handcuffing several people and taking them away during the operation.
DB chief Shafiqul Islam added that the DMP will take legal action if any violation of the law is found during the investigation.
When asked if a minister could perform police duties, the DB chief declined to comment.
caption:
A State Minister brandishing firearms during a 'drug raid'? The DMP is now investigating.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has ordered an investigation into the brandishing of firearms by State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain and his associates.

The probe follows videos uploaded by the minister himself to his verified Facebook page, showing him carrying a firearm while chasing people during a drive in Gandaria.

DMP Detective Branch chief Shafiqul Islam stated that the deputy commissioner of the DMP's Wari Division has been assigned to investigate the incident.

In one video, captioned 'Ishraque's action: Drug dens demolished, dealers handed over to police', the minister and another individual were seen carrying firearms.

Another video showed police handcuffing several people and taking them away during the operation.

DB chief Shafiqul Islam added that the DMP will take legal action if any violation of the law is found during the investigation.

When asked if a minister could perform police duties, the DB chief declined to comment.
